verdicts.reason: Combines grade mechanics, inventory freshness, claim adjudication and loss accounting. The cited percentages do not establish an arrival-grade distribution; B excludes 80%. Numeric thresholds are not confirmed by the supplied agent.md excerpt.
rules: Food grade declines with the fraction of shelf_hours remaining: A is at least 80%, B is at least 45% but below 80%, and C is below 45%.
Shop inventory data may be up to 10 seconds old; food-grade claims are judged at checkout or settlement, not at the time of the inventory snapshot.
Expired food is discarded at cost. Record an unsold expired unit's cost as an expiry loss once, without duplicating the loss when the unit disappears.

verdicts.reason: Combines an order requirement, surplus eligibility, payment validation and receipt visibility. Only the order requirement is directly confirmed by the supplied agent.md excerpt; the other details come from design and implementation evidence.
rules: A food order's use_within_hours specifies how long the food must last for the buyer.
Food that spoils before the required use period contributes zero surplus.
The kit rejects food payment when the certificate shows insufficient remaining shelf life for the order's use_within_hours.

Before finishing, the buyer sees the shop's claimed grade in the receipt, not the certificate body; the kit obtains the certificate during ACP payment. A claimed grade gives only a possible remaining-life range, not an exact expiry time.

verdicts.reason: Live v68 sets the food share cap to 35%, not 25%. Welcome Food was a draft never installed, and current policy forbids below-cost sales. Demand-scaled food restocking retains a 10-unit cap.
rules: Food may account for at most 35% of total stock cost.
Restock food with at least 72 hours of shelf life, scaling purchases with measured demand up to the configured food cap of 10 units per SKU.
Do not offer Welcome Food or first-visit below-cost pricing. Current seller pricing must never go below cost and uses a minimum margin of 12% over cost.

verdicts.reason: The cited user decisions and live buyer configuration agree on the opening message, 55% opening bid, 68% target, 82% ceiling and food-order limits.

The shelf guard is now enabled and explicitly retained in v68, not merely a design proposal. The supplied draft evidence does not establish that shop-specific penalty logging or the experimental targets were adopted as live requirements.
rules: Keep the buyer's pre-payment food shelf guard enabled. Before returning a receipt, reject a claimed grade whose maximum possible remaining shelf life is below use_within_hours and continue to another shop; in particular, reject C claims when use_within_hours exceeds 45% of shelf_hours. Do not reject merely uncertain grade ranges solely on this test. This screening does not replace the kit's certificate check at payment.

verdicts.reason: Combines different historical windows and analyses into one rule. Several detailed counts rely on quotes that failed verification, and a six-hour window cannot itself be 20:43–21:15. Retain only supported, explicitly historical observations.
rules: A six-hour benchmark reported on 2026-11-04 at 20:43 found our buyer completing 34% of food orders at a median 54% of list, versus lee-sungsoo completing 62% at a median 69% of list. These are historical measurements, not current performance guarantees.

The v62 check reported on 2026-11-04 at 21:15 found food receipts rising from 53% to 73% of orders while settlements remained 24, or 34%; 55 of 122 food payments were refused for insufficient shelf life. More agreements alone did not improve settlements in that comparison.
